verdict: SCI-PLEX SATURATION TEST (K562, 24h, 188 drugs x 4 doses, graded chemical titration) -- HONEST split result: one half confirmed, the other NOT. Q1 CONFIRMED -- response MAGNITUDE scales with dose: median Spearman(log dose, n_movers) = 0.4, and 71% of drugs show magnitude rising with dose (more choke -> bigger response), extending the K562-knockout magnitude finding (~0.5) to graded chemical perturbation. Q2 NOT SUPPORTED -- no dose-invariant program: low-vs-high profile Spearman 0.007 (~0), and even between the two highest both-responding doses only 0.022 (~0). Either the program reorganises with dose or (more likely) per-drug pseudobulk profiles are too noisy for a stable-program rank-correlation to survive (only HDAC/CDK inhibitors drive big responses). I will NOT claim program stability. NET: Sci-Plex confirms MAGNITUDE is dose-tunable (the predictable axis) but does NOT here demonstrate a fixed dose-invariant identity program -- 'dose predicts how big', 'which genes' stays the hard part. Downloaded via scPerturb/Zenodo (Sci-Plex 3).
